# Version 4.159.0 (Unreleased)
> **Image comparison and rendering refinements**

## Highlights

SkiaSharp 4.159.0 introduces an experimental image comparison package for rendering tests. SkiaSharp.Testing provides configurable acceptance policies and difference images. Ganesh texture-edge sampling and Tizen CPU blur selection also change, and Linux x86 native assets are no longer packaged.

## Breaking Changes

- **Move Linux x86 deployments to a supported architecture** — Linux x86 native assets are no longer built or included in NuGet packages. Move deployments that depend on linux-x86 assets to a supported Linux architecture before upgrading. ([#5784](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5784))

## API Surface

- **Experimental image comparison package** — SkiaSharp.Testing compares SKImage, SKBitmap and SKPixmap inputs with channel tolerances, masks, mismatch budgets and error metrics, and creates independent caller-owned difference images. The assembly is experimental; opt in by suppressing SKIA4001 with NoWarn or a pragma. ([#5293](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5293))

## Engine

- **Keep filtered texture samples inside subset boundaries** — Ganesh sampling now uses an inward offset to avoid including undefined texels outside a texture subset. Texture-edge pixels may differ; CPU and Graphite rendering are unchanged by this sampling option. ([#5679](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5679))
- **Align Tizen CPU blur selection** — Tizen now applies its CPU blur option to Skia itself, selecting the existing ThreeBoxApprox/Tent paths instead of the shader-based Gaussian candidate. Blur pixels and performance may differ; Tizen rendering and performance have not been measured locally. ([#5679](https://github.com/mono/SkiaSharp/pull/5679))
